analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new 'Native Flint' section in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1742-1868) and a 'Flint memory admission' section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 516-558). No executable code, key handling, attestation, coordinator or provider wire contract, or policy is changed. Unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:0 is a metadata-only entry with no line content, and I found nothing security-relevant in it.

I checked the described behavior against the threat model. It describes a native Flint model adapter with a strict loader that rejects missing, extra or duplicate tensors and unsupported geometry (relevant to T-012/T-027, weights integrity). The adapter requires native KV and checkpoint precision, and it adds a token-level protocol constraint covering reasoning/tool-call boundaries. It documents bounded caches and states: 8192 maximum states, four cache entries, 1024-byte maximum key size, JSON depth 128, and 65,536 bytes of raw-string key metadata. The constraint fails closed on state-pool exhaustion, and Flint memory admission adds no activation or OS reserve exception. The documents state that context overflow returns HTTP 400 before any SSE headers. They also state that arguments containing a literal </arg_value> are rejected and malformed frames fail closed.

These are descriptions of source I cannot see (FlintNativeProtocolConstraint, ToolConstraintFactory, FlintRequestPolicy, the memory-admission integration). I cannot verify that the code matches the claims. Open questions for later passes are whether the per-request mask caches are bounded under adversarial consumer prompts (T-010-style DoS), whether Flint SSD prefix-cache behavior (T-041) is unchanged, and whether the prompt-normalization v9 mirror in the platform is consistent. The doc also notes that the unconstrained diagnostic path does not reflect production. The doc cross-links point to immutable platform commits.

No new attack surface or invalidated assumption is established by the supplied evidence, so I report no findings.
